chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abdillah ibn Muskān, who said: Abān al-Azraq narrated to me from Zurārah, from Abū Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
"Whoever does not find the sacrificial animal (al-hady) and wishes to fast the three days at the beginning of the ten [days of Dhul-Hijjah], there is no objection to that."

And it is not permissible for a man to shave his head or visit the House (Kaaba) except after the sacrifice or until 'the sacrificial animal reaches its place of destination', which is that he buys it and places it on his mount. Narrated.

key_terms.الذَّبْحِ: The act of slaughtering the sacrificial animal
key_terms.الْعَشْرِ: The first ten days of the month of Dhul-Hijjah
key_terms.الْهَدْيَ: The sacrificial animal offered by a pilgrim during Hajj
key_terms.يَبْلُغَ الْهَدْيُ مَحِلَّهُ: The sacrificial animal reaches its destination/place

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for shaving the head and performing Tawaf if one cannot afford the Hajj sacrifice?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the alternative expiation for pilgrims lacking the means for *hady*, permitting the fasting of the first three days of Dhul-Hijjah. It establishes a strict condition that the pilgrim remains in the state of *Hajj* restrictions—specifically prohibiting head shaving and Tawaf—until the sacrifice is either performed or the animal arrives at its destination, ensuring the ritual obligation is fully satisfied before exiting the sacred state.
